body: claimed: issue-worker-high (Opus 5.5) · 2026-11-17T02:01Z · worktree/branch issue/2317-waterline-corner-arcs · plan: find the merge that stops the Waterline corner arcs, restore them, pin with corner_arc_radius

Escalation from issue-worker-high (Opus 5.5). The work is larger than `effort:high`. I raise the label to `effort:max` and release the claim.

## Cause (found)

PR #2273 (`d8c710f5f`) changed `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_emit.rs`. The `hold_fitted` condition now sends Waterline and Offset rings through `post_crossing_free`. When arc turns (#1733) are on, the runs that go there are the filleted walks.

`arc_cross::refuse` maps a walk back onto its pass with `arc_proof::judge`. The map uses the pass's own vertices. A filleted walk has new vertices, so `judge` returns `None`. Then `plain(pass)` removes every arc of that pass, the blends included. The note says `N could not be proved inside the cutter-centre area`.

Readings on the `corner_arc_radius` island pocket at `r = 1 mm`, on main `034c37842`:

- Waterline: 6 arcs, no blend arc. The test fails here.
- Offset rings: 0 arcs of 102. The test also fails here, but the loop stops at Waterline first.

These conditions make the law refuse a filleted pass:

1. A fitted arc of the Waterline pass truly crosses another feed.
2. A blend arc of radius 0.5 mm ends tangent on the line y = 7, where a leg of a different pass runs on the same line. The arc centre is on the 1 um lattice (`31.629868, 7.5`). Because of this, a bracket vertex is 7e-8 mm below y = 7. The strict predicate in `arc_cross::crosses` reads this as a crossing. `verify::crossed_pairs` at 0.01 mm and at 0.0005 mm finds no crossing there.
3. With blends at the tool radius (`blend_radius: None`), Waterline blends truly cross other feeds. `verify::crossed_pairs` gives the pairs `[3,10] [12,20] [64,71] [73,81]`. Main refuses these passes today, and that is correct.

## Why I stop

A fix must keep condition 3 refused and let condition 2 stand. The law on the filleted walks must stay. But that law must then tell a lattice-noise tangent touch from a real crossing. This is a change to the crossing law (`arc_cross`, which the HSM plan and the 3D ladder also use), or a per-blend refusal map for filleted walks. Both are collision-law design (`effort:max`).

## Held work

Branch `issue/2317-waterline-corner-arcs`, commit `51c4d8767c67dcfc722f03240a2c48a508835a89`. Do not merge it.

- `arc_cross::crossing_free_runs`: holds the law on the plain fit and returns the walks that stand.
- `pocket_emit`: for Waterline and Offset rings with blends, holds the law on the plain fit and rounds the arcs that stand. The second law round on the filleted walks is removed. That removal is not safe: it brings back condition 3.
- New pinning test `the_crossing_law_keeps_the_arc_turns_and_crosses_nowhere` in `crates/motion/tests/corner_arc_radius.rs`. It fails on the held commit for Waterline `r=None` (condition 3). Keep this test for the real fix.
- `docs/decisions/2317-blend-crossing-law.md` records the dropped options. The real fix must rewrite it.

A next step that I recommend: keep the first round (law on the plain fit) and also the second round on the filleted walks. Then make the second round refuse one blend at a time (back to the sharp corner of the stage-one walk), not the whole pass. Then decide if a touch at the arc's end, within the 1 um lattice, is a crossing.

Tests on the held commit: motion `--lib` 403 passed. `corner_blend`, `corner_blend_arc_contour`, `machining2d`, `rest2d`, `rest_zigzag`, `level_links`, `xy_arc_entry`, `entry_arc`, `predrilled_entry`, `refusal_ghost`, `radial_step`, `climb_direction` and `center_cut_law` passed. `corner_arc_radius`: 7 passed, 1 failed (the new test). Clippy on `camcraft-motion` is clean.

fix on issue/2317-blend-crossing-law · PR #2323 · pinned by the_crossing_law_keeps_the_arc_turns_and_crosses_nowhere, corners_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius, only_a_chord_on_the_end_tangent_is_a_touch · merges when reviewed

The law now refuses one corner arc, not the pass. A tangent touch of a corner arc within 1e-5 mm is not a crossing. No golden of `golden_cl` moved. The decision is in `docs/decisions/2317-blend-crossing-law.md`.
